# String literals that contain a bank entry name but are not provider
# knowledge. Matched against the WHOLE literal, case-insensitively — never a
# substring, so exempting one URL cannot accidentally exempt a family of them.
#
# Adding a line here weakens TestNoBankEntryKnowledgeInSource, which is why it
# is a file and not a rule embedded in the test: it makes weakening the check a
# visible diff that a reviewer can object to.
#
# Before adding anything, be sure the literal is genuinely incidental. If the
# CLI is branching on it, formatting it into a path, or looking it up, that is
# the coupling this test exists to catch and the fix is to move the knowledge
# into the bank.

https://github.com/lpezet/secure-agent-lab
https://github.com/lpezet/secure-agent-lab-cli

# internal/bank fetches the stack over HTTPS rather than by clone. These name
# the host the stack repo happens to be published on, and the media type its
# API speaks. Both would be equally true if the bank were empty — which is the
# test for whether a literal is provider knowledge or not.
https://api.github.com
https://codeload.github.com
application/vnd.github+json

# The git source each service in a generated compose file builds from. Same
# reasoning: it names where the stack is published, not anything about a
# provider. Note that the RENDERED output is checked separately by
# internal/compose's TestNoProviderNamesInOutput, which this file cannot cover
# because the AST walk never reads a template.
https://github.com/lpezet/secure-agent-lab.git

# internal/source parses a GitHub repository reference, and internal/cli's
# `providers source` explains what it accepts. These name the HOST a third-party
# providers repository is published on, which is the same reason the entries
# above are here — and the same test applies: every one of them would be
# equally true if the bank were empty, and none of them is looked up, branched
# on, or formatted into a path for a provider called github.
#
# Worth noting the near-miss: the bank DOES carry an entry called `github`, and
# these literals have nothing to do with it. That is exactly why the check
# matches whole literals and exempting is a visible diff.
https://github.com/
http://github.com/
github.com/
git@github.com:

# Note what is NOT here: any prose. Three help and error strings named the host
# in a sentence, and exempting a sentence works until somebody rewords it — the
# check would go quiet without anyone deciding it should. The host is named in
# the four prefixes above instead, and every message interpolates the first of
# them.
